findings.message: The Scope in and the first acceptance criterion require the named test's green rerun to be "observed through `resolution.link`". In Context, `Resolution` is `{link, note, resolved_at}`, and the Author path sets `link` to the authored fix stem. A stem link cannot hold a test-rerun observation, so no implementation can meet this criterion faithfully. The ticket also says the box resolution "status" must name `fix_stem`, but `Message.status` is the closed Literal `pending|authored|tombstoned|decided` and cannot name a stem.
findings.paved_road: Split the two prerequisites. (1) Fix identity: `Box.get(box_id)` has `status == "authored"` and `resolution.link == fix_stem` exactly, never inferred from a stem name. (2) Green rerun: a separate observation of the named `test_id` that the release call receives as an explicit input. Rewrite the Scope in and the first criterion to match, and keep one no-release case per prerequisite: wrong status, link mismatch, unmerged stem, and missing or red rerun.

findings.message: Two release reads have no named source. The "that exact stem must have merged" check reads a merge fact without naming the journal event that proves it or the module that emits it. The green-rerun read names no producer at all, and no merged or seeded ticket in the plane emits a per-test rerun result. An implementer would have to invent both formats, which breaks the rule that every read names a merged or seeded source.
findings.paved_road: Name the merge evidence as the existing journal `state_transition` to `merged` for `fix_stem`, read through `squatch.journal` (already Context). Make the green-rerun observation a typed argument the dormant hook's caller supplies, and state that production supply belongs to the later activation. The fenced `tests/test_flake.py` then fabricates both inputs directly.

findings.message: Scope in makes `journal-roll` and `storm-ledger` both depend only on `phase3-continue-15`, which lets `storm-ledger` run in parallel with `journal-roll`. Section 20's registry lists the pair as `journal-roll`, then `storm-ledger`. Every committed seed from an earlier pair written that way depends on its predecessor: `dispatch-config-snapshot` on `dispatch-admission-boundary`, `control-inbox` on `background-consumers`, `rework-activation` on `merge-queue-activation`, and `kill-failure-suppression` on `kill-worker-stop`. Making `tests/test_journal.py` read-only preservation for `storm-ledger` also assumes the journal module `journal-roll` changes. So the pinned edges contradict the registry order, and the seeded test would lock in a wrong edge.
findings.paved_road: Make `journal-roll` depend on `phase3-continue-15` and `storm-ledger` depend on `journal-roll`. Keep `phase3-continue-16` depending on both. Pin these edges in the BATCH mapping of `tests/test_seeded_phase3_15.py`, and state them the same way in Scope in and in the acceptance criteria.

Flake-boundary clarification: `flake-detection` and `flake-release` implement section 11.5's test quarantine ledger; they never invent a SHA-held set. Detection is called only after one named check test fails and then passes on the bare same-workspace/no-code-change re-run. Given `test_id`, the signature-deduped report `signature`, and the resulting Suggestion Box `box_id`, it appends one `signal` event keyed `flake/<box_id>` with body `{kind: flake_detected, test_id, signature, box_id}` and folds that test into quarantine. Detection itself is dormant construction through a `compose_daemon_flake`-style hook in `squatch/daemon.py`; no production composition in `squatch/__main__.py` or `squatch/drain.py` calls or constructs it yet, though `squatch.flake` may be import-reachable through daemon composition.

Mechanical release is identity-bound to the SAME ledger entry: the box resolution status for `box_id` must name `fix_stem`, that exact stem must have merged, and the named test's green rerun must be observed. It appends one `signal` event keyed `flake-release/<box_id>/<fix_stem>` with body `{kind: flake_released, test_id, signature, box_id, fix_stem}` BEFORE folding the entry out of quarantine. A second release of the same identity appends no event and changes no state. The direct release-hook proof lives in fenced `tests/test_flake.py`; existing production composition tests remain unchanged preservation suites unless a later activation actually calls the hook.
